<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><u>Exit Credit Facility</u></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">On November 14, 2017, GulfMark Rederi AS, or Rederi, a subsidiary of GulfMark Offshore, Inc., entered into an agreement, or the Credit Facility Agreement, with DNB Bank ASA, New York Branch, as agent, DNB Capital LLC as revolving and swingline lender, and certain funds managed by Hayfin Capital Management LLP as term lenders, providing for two credit facilities: a senior secured revolving credit facility, or the Revolving Credit Facility, and a senior secured term loan facility, or the Term Loan Facility (or, together, the Facilities). The Revolving Credit Facility provides $25 million of borrowing capacity, including $12.5 million for swingline loans and $5.0 million for letters of credit. The Term Loan Facility provides a $100 million term loan, which was funded in full on the November 14, 2017. Borrowings under the Revolving Credit Facility may be denominated in U.S. Dollars, NOK, GBP and Euros. Both Facilities mature on November 14, 2022.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
<div id="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">53</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; border: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000">
<div id="PGHDR" style="text-align: left; width: 100%">&nbsp;</div>
</div>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Borrowings under the Facilities accrue interest on U.S. Dollar borrowings at our option using either (i)&nbsp;the adjusted U.S. prime rate, or ABR, plus 5.25%, or (ii) the LIBOR Rate plus 6.25%. NOK loans substitute LIBOR with an adjusted Norwegian offered quotation rate for deposits in NOK and Euro loans substitute LIBOR with an adjusted euro interbank offered rate administered by the European Money Markets Institute.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Repayment of borrowings under the Facilities is guaranteed by GulfMark Offshore, Inc. and each of its significant subsidiaries (or, collectively, with Rederi, the Obligors), and is secured by a lien on 27 collateral vessels, or the Collateral Vessels, and substantially all other assets of the Obligors.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Commitments under the Revolving Credit Facility will be reduced beginning on November 14, 2020 in semiannual increments of approximately $3.1 million until maturity. The Term Loan Facility is payable in semiannual installments beginning on November 14, 2020 and based on a five-year level principal payment schedule, payable semiannually.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Term Loan Facility prepayments prior to November 14, 2019 are subject to a make-whole premium based on the present value of interest otherwise payable from the prepayment date forward. Prepayments on or after November 14, 2019 and prior to November 14, 2020 are subject to a 2% premium. Mandatory prepayments, other than those triggered by a casualty event, are subject to prepayment premiums. Mandatory prepayments are required upon the occurrence of certain events including, but not limited to, a change of control or the sale or total loss of a Collateral Vessel. Prepayments of the Revolving Credit Facility are not materially restricted or penalized.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">The Credit Facility Agreement was evaluated for embedded derivatives that must be bifurcated and separately accounted for as freestanding derivatives. The Term Loan Facility and Revolving Credit Facility are not derivatives and are not measured at fair value. Therefore, the nature of any embedded features must be analyzed to determine whether each feature requires bifurcation by both (1) meeting the definition of a derivative and (2) not being considered clearly and closely related to the host contract. We have identified three features in the Credit Facility Agreement that are considered embedded derivatives. There is a contingent interest feature related to default interest, a breakage costs potential not related to prepayments, and certain potential contingent payments related to increased costs caused by changes in law. We determined that the value of these features are de minimis at the inception of the agreement and that we do not foresee events that would require a value adjustment in our consolidated financial statements. We will continue to assess the likelihood of triggering events and to the extent they are determined to be material, these features will be bifurcated from the debt instrument and subsequently marked to fair value through earnings.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">The Credit Facility Agreement contains financial covenants that require that we maintain: (i) minimum liquidity of $30.0 million, including $15.0 million in cash, (ii) a leverage ratio (total debt to 12 months EBITDA) of not more than 5.0 to 1.0, tested quarterly beginning December 31, 2020, (iii) a total debt to capital ratio, tested quarterly, not to exceed 0.45 to 1.0, and (iv) a collateral to commitment coverage ratio of at least 2.50 to 1.0. The Credit Facility Agreement contains a number of restrictions that limit our ability to, among other things, sell Collateral Vessels, borrow money, make investments, incur additional liens on assets, buy or sell assets, merge, or pay dividends and contain a number of potential events of default related to our business, financial condition and vessel operations.</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> Collateral Vessel operations are also subject to a variety of restrictive provisions. Proceeds from borrowings under the Credit Facility Agreement may not be used to acquire vessels or finance business acquisitions generally. At December 31, 2017, we were in compliance with all of the financial covenants under the Credit Facility Agreement.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We execute letters of credit, performance bonds and other guarantees in the normal course of business that ensure our performance or payments to third parties. We had<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> $3.2 million in letters of credit outstanding at December<b>&nbsp;</b>31, 2017. In the past, no significant claims have been made against these financial instruments. We believe the likelihood of demand for payment is minimal and expect no material cash outlays to occur from these instruments.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Currency Fluctuations and Inflation</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:14.4pt;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">A majority of our operations are international; <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">therefore, we are exposed to currency fluctuations and exchange rate risks. Charters for vessels in our North Sea fleet are primarily denominated in GBP, with a portion denominated in NOK or Euros. In areas where currency risks are potentially high, we normally accept only a small percentage of charter hire in local currency, with the remainder payable in U.S.<b> </b>Dollars. Operating costs are substantially denominated in the same currency as charter hire in order to reduce the risk of currency fluctuations. The North Sea fleet generated 58% of our total consolidated revenue for the combined Successor and Predecessor periods in 2017.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:14.4pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:14.4pt;">In 201<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">7, the exchange rates of GBP, NOK, Euro, BRL and SGD against the U.S.<b> &nbsp;</b>Dollar ranged as follows:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Our outstanding debt is denominated in U.S.<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b>&nbsp;</b>Dollars, but a substantial portion of our revenue is generated in currencies other than the U.S.<b>&nbsp;</b>Dollar. We have evaluated these conditions and have determined that it is not in our interest to use any financial instruments to hedge this exposure under present conditions. Our strategy is in part based on a number of factors including the following:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

			<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;font-size:10pt;">the cost of using hedging instruments in relation to the risks of currency fluctuations;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">One or more of these factors may change and, in response, we may begin to use financial instruments to hedge risks of currency fluctuations. We may from time to time hedge known liabilities denominated in foreign currencies to reduce the effects of exchange rate fluctuations on our financial results. We do not use foreign currency forward contracts for trading or speculative purposes.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:54pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Reflected in the accompanying consolidated balance sheet at December<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b>&nbsp;</b>31, 2017, is a $3.0 million gain in accumulated other comprehensive income relating to the change in exchange rates at December<b>&nbsp;</b>31, 2017 in comparison to the exchange rate at the date of our emergence from bankruptcy. Changes in the accumulated other comprehensive income are non-cash items that are primarily attributable to investments in vessels and U.S.<b>&nbsp;</b>Dollar-based capitalization between our parent company and our foreign subsidiaries. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">To date, general inflationary trends have not had a material effect on our operating revenues or expenses.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>New Accounting Pronouncements</b></p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>I</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b>TEM 7A. </b><i><b>Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk</b></i></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> information included in this Item 7A is considered to constitute &ldquo;forward-looking statements&rdquo; for purposes of the statutory safe harbor provided in Section 27A of the Securities Act and Section 21E of the Exchange Act. See &ldquo;Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements.&rdquo; </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Financial Instruments</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We are subject to financial market risks, including fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates and interest rates. In order to manage and mitigate our exposure to these risks, we may use derivative financial instruments in accordance with established policies and procedures. At <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">December&nbsp;31, 2017, we had no outstanding derivative contracts. Refer to Note&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">1 &ldquo;Nature of Operations and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies&mdash;</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Fair Value of Financial Instruments&rdquo; to our Consolidated Financial Statements included in Part II, Item<b>&nbsp;</b>8 &ldquo;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data&rdquo; for additional information on financial instruments. </font></p>

<p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>F</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b>oreign Currency Risk</b> </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The functional currency for the majority of our international operations is that operation<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s local currency. Adjustments resulting from the translation of the local functional currency financial statements to the U.S.&nbsp;Dollar, which is based on current exchange rates, are included in the Consolidated Statements of Stockholders&rsquo; Equity as a separate component of &ldquo;Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (Loss).&rdquo; Working capital of our international operations may in part be held or denominated in a currency other than the local currency, and gains and losses resulting from holding those balances are included in the Consolidated Statements of Operations in &ldquo;</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Foreign currency loss and other&rdquo; in the current period. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We operate in a number of international areas and are involved in transactions denominated in currencies other than U.S. Dollars, which exposes us to foreign currency exchange<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> rate risk. At various times we may utilize forward exchange contracts, local currency borrowings and the payment structure of customer contracts to selectively hedge exposure to exchange rate fluctuations in connection with monetary assets, liabilities and cash flows denominated in certain foreign currencies. See Part II, Item<b>&nbsp;</b>7 &ldquo;Management&rsquo;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations &ndash; Currency Fluctuations and Inflation.&rdquo; Other than trade accounts receivable and trade accounts payable, we do not currently have financial instruments that are sensitive to foreign currency exchange rates.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We transact business in various foreign currencies which subjects our cash flows and earnings to exposure related to changes in foreign currency exchange rates. We <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">generally attempt to manage this exposure through operational strategies and not through the use of foreign currency forward exchange contracts. We do not engage in hedging activity for speculative or trading purposes. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">From time to time, <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">however, we may hedge firmly committed, anticipated transactions in the normal course of business and these contracts are designated and qualify as fair value hedges. Changes in the fair value of derivatives that are designated as fair value hedges are deferred in the Consolidated Statements of Stockholders&rsquo; Equity as a separate component of &ldquo;Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income&rdquo; until the underlying transactions occur. At such time, the related deferred hedging gains or losses are recorded on the same line as the hedged item. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Net<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> foreign currency losses, including derivative activity, for the combined Predecessor and Successor 2017 periods and the Predecessor years ended December&nbsp;31, 2016 and 2015 were $0.4 million, $2.4 million and $1.1 million, respectively. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>In</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b>t</b><b>erest Rate</b><b> Risk</b> </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We are subject to market risk for changes in interest rates related primarily to our long-term debt. The following table, which presents principal cash flows by expected maturity dates and weighted average interest rates, summarizes our fixed and variable rate debt obligations at December<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;31, 2017 (Successor) and at December 31, 2016 (Predecessor) that are sensitive to changes in interest rates. The floating portion of our variable rate debt is based on the adjusted U.S. prime rate, LIBOR and certain market rates related to the NOK and the Euro, depending on which currency we designate to borrow funds.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>ITEM 8. </b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><i><b>Financial Statements and Supplementary Data</b></i> </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</b></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">To the Stockholders and Board of Directors<br>
<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">GulfMark Offshore, Inc.:</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><i>Opinion on the Consolidated Financial Statements</i></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of GulfMark Offshore, Inc. and<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;consolidated subsidiaries (the Company) as of December&nbsp;31, 2017 (Successor) and 2016 (Predecessor), the related consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive income (loss), stockholders&rsquo; equity, and cash flows for the periods of November 15, 2017 to December 31, 2017 (Successor), January 1, 2017 to November 14, 2017 (Predecessor), and for the years ended December 31, 2016 and 2015 (Predecessor), and the related notes (collectively, the consolidated financial statements). In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of December&nbsp;31, 2017 (Successor) and 2016 (Predecessor), and the results of its operations and its cash flows for the periods of November 15, 2017 to December 31, 2017 (Successor), January 1, 2017 to November 14, 2017 (Predecessor) and for the years ended December 31, 2016 and 2015 (Predecessor), in conformity with U.S.&nbsp;generally accepted accounting principles.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><i>New Basis of Presentation</i></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">As discussed in Note<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;1 to the consolidated financial statements, on October 4, 2017, the United States Bankruptcy Court in the District of Delaware entered an order confirming the Company&rsquo;s plan for reorganization under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code, which became effective on November 14, 2017. Accordingly, the accompanying consolidated financial statements have been prepared in conformity with Accounting Standards Codification&nbsp;852-10, <i>Reorganizations</i>, for the Successor as a new entity with assets, liabilities and a capital structure having carrying amounts not comparable with prior periods as described in Note&nbsp;2.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><i>Basis for Opinion</i></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">These consolidated financial statements are the responsibility of the Company<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these consolidated financial statements based on our audits. We are a public accounting firm registered with the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (PCAOB) and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the consolidated financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. The Company is not required to have, nor were we engaged to perform, an audit of its internal control over financial reporting. As part of our audits, we are required to obtain an understanding of internal control over financial reporting but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the Company<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting. Accordingly, we express no such opinion.Our audits included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the consolidated financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the consolidated financial statements. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the consolidated financial statements. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">We have served as the Company<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s auditor since 2011.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="12868" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1522067186956" id="thunderdome-statement-849946">
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>(<em data-td-fact-id="29306334" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em>) NATURE OF OPERATIONS AND SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Nature of Operations</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">GulfMark Offshore, Inc. and its subsidiaries (collectively referred to as &ldquo;we&rdquo;, &ldquo;us&rdquo;, &ldquo;our&rdquo; or the &ldquo;Company&rdquo;) own and operate offshore supply vessels, principally in the North Sea, offshore Southeast Asia and offshore the Americas. The vessels provide transportation of materials, supplies and personnel to and from offshore platforms and drilling rigs. Some of these vessels also perform anchor handling and towing services<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">On <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> May 17, 2017, </em>GulfMark Offshore, Inc. filed a voluntary petition, or the <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Chapter <em data-td-fact-id="29306335" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">11</em> Case, under chapter <em data-td-fact-id="29306336" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">11</em> of title <em data-td-fact-id="29306337" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">11</em> of the United States Code, or the Bankruptcy Code, in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware, or the Bankruptcy Court. On <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> October 4, 2017, </em>the Bankruptcy Court entered an order, or the Confirmation Order, approving the Amended Chapter <em data-td-fact-id="29306338" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">11</em> Plan of Reorganization, as confirmed, or the Plan. On <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2017, </em>or the Effective Date, the Plan became effective pursuant to its terms and we emerged from the Chapter <em data-td-fact-id="29306339" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">11</em> Case. For a more detailed discussion of our bankruptcy proceedings and our emergence from bankruptcy, see </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Note&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="29306340" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">On the Effective Date, we adopted and applied the relevant guidance with respect to the accounting and financial reporting for entities that have emerged from bankruptcy proceedings, or Fresh Start Accounting. Under Fresh Start Accounting, our balance sheet on the Effective Date reflects all of our assets and liabilities at their fair values. Our emergence and the adoption of Fresh Start Accounting resulted in a new reporting entity, or the Successor, for financial reporting purposes. To facilitate our discussion and analysis of our vessels, financial condition and results of operations herein, we refer to the reorganized company as the Successor for periods subsequent to <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2017 </em>and the Predecessor for periods prior to <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 15, 2017. </em>For a more detailed discussion, including the disclosure of our final Predecessor balance sheet as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2017 </em>and our beginning Successor balance sheet as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 15, 2017, </em>see</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> Note&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="29306341" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:14.4pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Principles of Consolidation</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Our consolidated financial statements include our accounts and those of our majority-owned subsidiaries. All significant inter-company accounts and transactions have been eliminated.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Use of Estimates</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:14.4pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America, or U.S. GAAP, requires us to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the consolidated financial statements and the reported amounts of revenue and expenses during the reporting period. The accompanying consolidated financial statements include significant estimates for allowance for doubtful accounts receivable, depreciable lives of vessels and equipment, income taxes and commitments and contingencies. While we believe current estimates are reasonable and appropriate, actual results could differ from these estimates.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:4.5pt;"><i>Cash and Cash Equivalents</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:14.4pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Our investments, consisting of U.S. Government securities and commercial paper with original maturities of up to <em data-td-fact-id="29306342" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> months, are included in cash and cash equivalents in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets and consolidated statements of cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Vessels and Equipment</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Vessels and equipment are stated at cost, net of accumulated depreciation, which is provided by the straight-line method over their estimated useful life. At the date of emergence from bankruptcy, we adopted new accounting policies to reflect our change in estimates related to useful lives of our vessels and estimated salvage value of our vessels. The Successor is depreciating the cost of our vessels over <em data-td-fact-id="29306343" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">20</em> years to an estimated salvage value of <em data-td-fact-id="29306344" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">five</em> percent of original cost. The Predecessor depreciated the cost of our vessels over <em data-td-fact-id="29306345" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">25</em> years to an estimated salvage value of <em data-td-fact-id="29306346" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">15</em> percent of original cost.</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> Interest is capitalized in connection with the construction of vessels. The capitalized interest is included as part of the asset to which it relates and is depreciated over the asset&rsquo;s estimated useful life. In<b>&nbsp;</b>the Successor <em data-td-fact-id="29306347" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> period we did <em data-td-fact-id="29306348" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> capitalize any interest. In the Predecessor <em data-td-fact-id="29306349" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> period we capitalized <em data-td-fact-id="29306350" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.1</em> million and in the Predecessor years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2016 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="29306351" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em> we capitalized <em data-td-fact-id="29306352" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$2.6</em> million and <em data-td-fact-id="29306353" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$5.0</em> million, respectively. Office equipment, furniture and fixtures, and vehicles are depreciated over <em data-td-fact-id="29306354" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">two</em> to <em data-td-fact-id="29306355" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">five</em> years. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:43.2pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
<div id="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">64</div>

</div>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">We incur significant costs for each vessel every <em data-td-fact-id="29306356" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">30</em> months for scheduled drydocks which are required to maintain our vessels in class. At the date of emergence from bankruptcy</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">, the Successor adopted an accounting policy whereby we capitalize drydock costs and amortize the expense over <em data-td-fact-id="29306357" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">30</em> months. The Predecessor expensed drydock costs as they were incurred.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:14.4pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:14.4pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Major renovation costs and modifications that extend the life or usefulness of the related assets are capitalized and depreciated over the assets&rsquo; estimated remaining useful lives. Maintenance and repair costs are expensed as incurred. Included in the consolidated statements of operations for the Successor <em data-td-fact-id="29306358" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> period is <em data-td-fact-id="29306359" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.5</em> million of maintenance and repairs. In the Predecessor <em data-td-fact-id="29306360" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> period and the Predecessor years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2016 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="29306361" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015,</em> we recorded <em data-td-fact-id="29306362" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$9.0</em> million, <em data-td-fact-id="29306363" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$9.3</em> million and <em data-td-fact-id="29306364" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$19.3</em><b>&nbsp;</b>million, respectively, of costs for maintenance and repairs.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We review long-lived assets for impairment whenever there is evidence that the carrying amount of such assets <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em><em data-td-fact-id="29306365" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> be recoverable. This <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">review consists of comparing the carrying amount of the asset with its expected future undiscounted cash flows before tax and interest costs. If the asset&rsquo;s carrying amount is less than such cash flow estimate, it is written down to its fair value on a discounted cash flow basis. Estimates of expected future cash flows represent management&rsquo;s best estimate based on currently available information and reasonable and supportable assumptions. Any impairment recognized is permanent and <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em><em data-td-fact-id="29306366" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> be restored. See Note <em data-td-fact-id="29306367" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">3</em> for the results of our impairment analyses.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Fair Value of Financial Instruments</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">O<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">ur financial instruments consist primarily of accounts receivable and payable (which are stated at carrying value which approximates fair value) and long-term debt. Periodically, we enter into forward derivative contracts to hedge our exposure to interest rate or foreign currency fluctuations. In the past, we have had open positions in such derivative contracts that are considered financial instruments for which we would disclose certain fair value information. As of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December</em><b>&nbsp;</b><em data-td-fact-id="29306368" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">31,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306369" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> for the Successor and <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2016 </em>for the Predecessor, there were <em data-td-fact-id="29306370" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> forward derivative open contracts. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Deferred Costs and Other Assets</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Deferred costs and other assets consist primarily of deferred financing costs<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> for revolving credit arrangements, deferred vessel mobilization costs and deferred drydock costs. Deferred financing costs are amortized over the expected term of the related debt. Should the debt for which a deferred financing cost has been recorded terminate by means of payment in full, tender offer or lender termination, the associated deferred financing costs would be immediately expensed. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:14.4pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">In connection with new long-term contracts, costs incurred that directly relate to mobilization of a vessel from <em data-td-fact-id="29306371" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> region to another are deferred and recognized over the primary contract term. Should either party terminate the contract prior to the end of the original contract term, the deferred amount would be immediately expensed. Costs of relocating vessels from <em data-td-fact-id="29306372" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> region to another without a contract are expensed as incurred.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Revenue Recognition</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Revenue from charters for offshore marine services is recognized as performed based on contractual charter rates and when collectability is reasonably assured. Currently, charter terms range from as short as several days to as long as <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="29306373" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">5</em><b>&nbsp;</b>years in duration. Management services revenue is recognized in the period in which the services are performed.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Income Taxes</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We recognize the amount of current year income taxes payable or refundable and deferred tax assets and liabilities for the expected future tax consequences of events that have been recognized in the financial statements or tax returns previously filed. Under this method, deferred tax assets and liabilities are determined based on the difference between the financial statement carrying amounts and tax bases of assets and liabilities using enacted tax rates and laws in effect for the years in which the differences are expected to reverse. The likelihood and amount of future taxable income and tax planning strategies are included in the criteria used to determine the timing and amount of net deferred tax assets recognized for net operating loss and tax credit carry-forwards in our consolidated financial statements. These deferred tax assets are, when appropriate, reduced by a valuation allowance resulting in net deferred tax assets that are more likely than <em data-td-fact-id="29306374" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> to be realized.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">A significant amount of judgment in our use of assumptions and estimates is required in our methodology for determining and recording income taxes. In some instances we use forecasts of expected operations and related tax implications and we consider the possibility of implementing tax planning strategies. Such variables can result in uncertainty and measurable variation between anticipated and actual results can occur. Changes to these variables as a result of unforeseen events <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>have a material impact on our income tax accounts.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
<div id="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">65</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; border: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000">

</div>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">In recent years we have had operations in over <em data-td-fact-id="29306375" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">40</em><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;countries and are or have been subject to a significant number of taxing jurisdictions. Our income earned in these jurisdictions is taxed on various bases, including actual income earned, deemed profits, and revenue based withholding taxes. Our income tax determinations involve the interpretation of applicable tax laws, tax treaties, and related tax rules and regulations of those jurisdictions. Changes in tax law, currency/repatriation controls and interpretation of local tax laws by the relevant tax authority could impact our income tax liabilities or assets in those jurisdictions.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">On <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December&nbsp;</em><em data-td-fact-id="29306376" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">22,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306377" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> the statute originally named the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, or the <em data-td-fact-id="29306378" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> Tax Act, was signed into law making significant changes to the Internal Revenue Code, or the Code. Changes include, but are <em data-td-fact-id="29306379" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> limited to, a federal corporate tax rate decrease from <em data-td-fact-id="29306380" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">35%</em> to <em data-td-fact-id="29306381" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">21%</em> for tax years beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December&nbsp;</em><em data-td-fact-id="29306382" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">31,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306383" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> as well as a <em data-td-fact-id="29306384" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em>-time transition tax related to the U.S. taxation of foreign earnings and profits that had <em data-td-fact-id="29306385" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> been previously taxed in the U.S. We have estimated our provision for income taxes in accordance with the <em data-td-fact-id="29306386" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> Tax Act guidance available as of the date of this report and as a result have recorded <em data-td-fact-id="29306387" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$15.2</em> million as additional income tax benefit in the <em data-td-fact-id="29306388" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">fourth</em> quarter of <em data-td-fact-id="29306389" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> the period in which the legislation was enacted.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">On <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 22, 2017, </em>Staff Accounting Bulletin <em data-td-fact-id="29306390" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306391" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">118,</em> or SAB <em data-td-fact-id="29306392" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">118,</em> was issued to address the application of U.S. GAAP in situations when a registrant does <em data-td-fact-id="29306393" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> have the necessary information available, prepared, or analyzed (including computations) in reasonable detail to complete the accounting for certain income tax effects of the <em data-td-fact-id="29306394" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> Tax Act. In accordance with SAB <em data-td-fact-id="29306395" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">118,</em> we have determined that the <em data-td-fact-id="29306396" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$15.2</em> million of the deferred tax benefit recorded in connection with the <em data-td-fact-id="29306397" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em>-time transition tax on foreign earnings and profits and the remeasurement of certain deferred tax assets and liabilities are provisional amounts and represent a reasonable estimate at <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017. </em>Any subsequent adjustment to these amounts will be recorded to income tax expense in the quarter of <em data-td-fact-id="29306398" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018</em> when the analysis is complete.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">In addition, we also account for uncertainty in income taxes by utilizing a more likely than <em data-td-fact-id="29306399" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not,</em> or greater than <em data-td-fact-id="29306400" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">50%</em> probability, minimum recognition threshold for measurement of a tax position taken or expected to be taken in a tax return that would be sustained upon examination by the relevant tax authorities. We recognize penalties and/or interest related to uncertain tax benefits as a component of income tax expense. Numerous factors contribute to our evaluation and estimation of our tax positions and related tax liabilities and /or benefits, which <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be adjusted periodically and <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be resolved differently than we anticipate. See Note <em data-td-fact-id="29306401" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">7.</em><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Foreign Currency Translation</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The local currencies of the majority of our foreign operations have been determined to be their functional currencies, except for certain foreign operations whose functional currency has been determined to be the U.S. Dollar, based on an assessment of the economic circumstances of the foreign operations. Assets and liabilities of our foreign affiliates are translated at year-end exchange rates, while revenue and expenses are translated at average rates for the period. As a result, amounts related to changes in assets and liabilities reported in the consolidated statements of cash flows will <em data-td-fact-id="29306402" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> necessarily agree to changes in the corresponding balances on the consolidated balance sheets. We consider most intercompany loans to be long-term investments; accordingly, the related translation gains and losses are reported as a component of stockholders<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo; equity. Transaction gains and losses are reported directly in the consolidated statements of operations. In the Successor <em data-td-fact-id="29306403" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> period, the Predecessor <em data-td-fact-id="29306404" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> period and during the Predecessor years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December</em><b>&nbsp;</b><em data-td-fact-id="29306405" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">31,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306406" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="29306407" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em> we reported net foreign currency losses in the amounts of <em data-td-fact-id="29306408" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.1</em> million, <em data-td-fact-id="29306409" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.3</em> million, <em data-td-fact-id="29306410" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$2.4</em><b>&nbsp;</b>million and <em data-td-fact-id="29306411" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.1</em><b>&nbsp;</b>million, respectively. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Concentration of Credit Risk</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We extend credit to various companies in the energy industry that <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be affected by changes in economic or other external conditions. Our policy is to manage our exposure to credit risk through credit approvals and limits. Our trade accounts receivable are aged based on contractual payment terms and an allowance for doubtful accounts is established in accordance with our written corporate policy. The age of the trade accounts receivable, customer collection history and management<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s judgment as to the customer&rsquo;s ability to pay are considered in determining whether an allowance is necessary. For the Successor period ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em>there were <em data-td-fact-id="29306412" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> significant write-offs or increases in our allowance for doubtful accounts and <em data-td-fact-id="29306413" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> customer accounted for <em data-td-fact-id="29306414" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">10%</em> or more of </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">the Successor&rsquo;s total consolidated revenue. For the Predecessor period ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2017, </em>the Predecessor reserved <em data-td-fact-id="29306415" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.0</em> million related to Southeast Asia and Americas customers and </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">had revenue from <em data-td-fact-id="29306416" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> customer in the Americas which accounted for <em data-td-fact-id="29306417" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">10%</em> or more of total consolidated revenue, totaling <em data-td-fact-id="29306418" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$9.0</em> million or <em data-td-fact-id="29306419" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">10.2%</em> of total consolidated revenue. </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">In <em data-td-fact-id="29306420" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016,</em> the Predecessor reserved <em data-td-fact-id="29306421" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.8</em> million related to <em data-td-fact-id="29306422" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> Southeast Asia customers. For the year ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2016, </em><em data-td-fact-id="29306423" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> customer accounted for <em data-td-fact-id="29306424" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">10%</em> or more of </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">the Predecessor&rsquo;s total consolidated revenue. </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">For the year ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December</em><b>&nbsp;</b><em data-td-fact-id="29306425" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">31,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306426" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015,</em> the Predecessor had revenue from <em data-td-fact-id="29306427" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> customer in the North Sea and <em data-td-fact-id="29306428" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> customer in the Americas which each accounted for <em data-td-fact-id="29306429" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">10%</em> or more of total consolidated revenue, totaling <em data-td-fact-id="29306430" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$32.4</em> million and <em data-td-fact-id="29306431" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$31.9</em> million, respectively, or <em data-td-fact-id="29306432" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">23.5%</em> of total consolidated revenue. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Stock-Based Compensation</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Predecessor had share-based compensation plans covering officers and other employees as well as the Predecessor Board of Directors. Stock-based grants made under the Predecessor<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s stock plans were recorded at fair value on the date of the grant and the cost was recognized ratably over the vesting period for the restricted stock and the stock options. The fair value of stock option awards was determined using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model. Restricted stock awards were valued using the market price of the Predecessor&rsquo;s Class A common stock on the grant date. Our stock-based compensation plans are more fully described in Note<b>&nbsp;</b><em data-td-fact-id="29306433" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">9.</em> </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:14.4pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div id="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">66</div>
