<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Our employee stock purchase plan would be considered compensatory whereby it allowed all of our U.S. employees and employees of participating subsidiaries to acquire shares of the Predecessor<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s Class A common stock at <em data-td-fact-id="29306434" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">85%</em> of the fair market value of the Class A common stock under a qualified plan as defined by Section<b>&nbsp;</b><em data-td-fact-id="29306435" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">423</em> of the Code. The employee stock purchase plan was terminated in the <em data-td-fact-id="29306436" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">first</em> quarter of <em data-td-fact-id="29306437" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Warrants</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We account for common stock warrants as either equity instruments or derivative liabilities depending on the specific terms of the warrant agreement.<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp; The warrants to acquire shares of Successor common stock at an exercise price of <em data-td-fact-id="29306438" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$.01</em> per share, or the Noteholder Warrants, and the warrants to acquire shares of Successor common stock at an exercise price of <em data-td-fact-id="29306439" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$100.00</em> per share, or the Equity Warrants, both qualify for the scope exception in Financial Accounting Standards Board, or FASB</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">, Accounting Standards Codification, or ASC, <em data-td-fact-id="29306440" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306441" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">815,</em> &ldquo;Derivatives and Hedging,&rdquo; for derivative accounting and therefore qualify for classification as equity.&nbsp; The equity scope exception is subject to review in each subsequent reporting period.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:7.2pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><i>Earnings Per Share</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Basic earnings per share, or EPS, is computed by dividing net income (loss) by the weighted average number of shares of common stock outstanding during the year. Diluted EPS is computed using the treasury stock method for common stock equivalents. The Successor issued Noteholder Warrants to purchase common stock to certain of holders of the Predecessor<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s long-term debt in the emergence from bankruptcy. The Noteholder Warrants have an exercise price of <em data-td-fact-id="29306442" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$.01</em> per share and are immediately exercisable. As a result, the Noteholder Warrants are considered to be outstanding shares of common stock and are included in the denominator of both basic and diluted EPS.&nbsp; The Equity Warrants issued to the Predecessor&rsquo;s stockholders are <em data-td-fact-id="29306443" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> participating securities and do <em data-td-fact-id="29306444" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> impact basic EPS prior to exercise.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Reclassifications</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Certain reclassifications of previously reported information have been made to conform to the current year presentation.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>New Accounting Pronouncements </i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> May 2014, </em>the <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">FASB,</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> issued Accounting Standards Update, or ASU, </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="29306445" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2014</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="29306446" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09,</em> &ldquo;Revenue from Contracts with Customers.&rdquo; The ASU will replace most existing revenue recognition guidance in U.S. GAAP. The core principle of the new standard is that a company will recognize revenue when it transfers control of promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration to which the company expects to be entitled in exchange for these goods or services. We have determined that the adoption of this standard will <em data-td-fact-id="29306447" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> have a material effect on our financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows. We are adopting this standard effective <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018 </em>using the retrospective option with practical expedients. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:7.2pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> February 2016, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="29306448" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="29306449" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">02,</em> &ldquo;Leases&rdquo; to increase transparency and comparability among organizations by recognizing all leases on the balance sheet and disclosing key information about leasing arrangements. The main difference between current accounting standards and ASU <em data-td-fact-id="29306450" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="29306451" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">02</em> is the recognition of assets and liabilities by lessees for those leases classified as operating leases under current accounting standards. While we are continuing to assess all potential impacts of these standards, we expect the measurement and recording of our revenues related to the offshore marine support and transportation services to remain substantially unchanged. However, the actual revenue recognition treatment required under the new standard <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be dependent on contract-specific terms and <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>vary in some instances. The new standard is effective for fiscal years beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2018. </em>We intend to adopt the new lease standard on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2019.</em></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> August 2016, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="29306452" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="29306453" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">15,</em> &ldquo;Statement of Cash Flows<b> </b>Classification of Certain Cash Receipts and Cash Payments.&rdquo; The objective of the new standard is to eliminate diversity in practice related to the classification of certain cash receipts and payments by adding or clarifying guidance on <em data-td-fact-id="29306454" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">eight</em> classification issues related to the statement of cash flows. This standard is effective for annual and interim periods in fiscal years beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2017. </em>The standard should be applied retrospectively to all periods presented. The adoption of this standard will <em data-td-fact-id="29306455" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> have a material effect on our financial condition or results of operations. We are adopting this standard effective <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:7.2pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> October 2016, </em>the FASB&nbsp;issued ASU&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="29306456" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="29306457" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">16,</em> &ldquo;Income Taxes, Intra-Entity Transfers of Assets Other Than Inventory.&rdquo; This standard requires recognition of tax consequences in the period in which a transfer takes place, with the exception of inventory transfers. There will be an immediate effect on earnings if the tax rates in the tax jurisdictions of the selling entity and buying entity are different. The new standard is effective for fiscal years beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2017. </em>The adoption of this standard will <em data-td-fact-id="29306458" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> have a material effect on our financial condition or results of operations. We are adopting this standard effective <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 2016, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="29306459" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="29306460" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">18</em><i>, &ldquo;Statement of Cash Flows (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="29306461" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">230</em>):&nbsp; Restricted Cash</i>&rdquo;.&nbsp; The ASU is intended to reduce diversity in the presentation of restricted cash and restricted cash equivalents in the statement of cash flows and requires that restricted cash and restricted cash equivalents be included as components of total cash and cash equivalents as presented on the statement of cash flows.&nbsp; The new standard is effective for fiscal years beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2017.&nbsp; </em>The adoption of this standard will <em data-td-fact-id="29306462" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> have a material effect on our financial condition or results of operations.&nbsp;&nbsp; We are adopting this standard <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 2017, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="29306463" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="29306464" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">01,</em> &ldquo;Business Combinations - Clarifying the Definition of a Business&rdquo;</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> to clarify the definition of a business with the objective of adding guidance to assist entities with evaluating whether transactions should be accounted for as acquisitions (or disposals) of assets or businesses. The definition of a business affects many areas of accounting including acquisitions, disposals, goodwill and consolidation. ASU <em data-td-fact-id="29306465" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="29306466" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">01</em> is effective in annual periods beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2017. </em>The adoption of this standard will <em data-td-fact-id="29306467" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> have a material effect on our financial condition or results of operations. We are adopting this standard effective <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018.</em></font></p>
</div>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:7.2pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="12869" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1522067222877" id="thunderdome-statement-849947">
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>(<em data-td-fact-id="29306468" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em>) EMERGENCE FROM BANKRUPTCY PROCEEDINGS AND FRESH START ACCOUNTING</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">On <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> May 17, 2017, </em>GulfMark Offshore, Inc. filed the <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Chapter <em data-td-fact-id="29306469" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">11</em> Case under the Bankruptcy Code in the Bankruptcy Court, and on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> October 4, 2017, </em>the Bankruptcy Court entered the Confirmation Order approving the Plan. On the Effective Date, <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2017, </em>the Plan became effective pursuant to its terms and we emerged from the Chapter <em data-td-fact-id="29306470" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">11</em> Case.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><i>Fresh Start Accounting</i></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:72pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">We adopted Fresh Start Accounting on the Effective Date in connection with our emergence from bankruptcy. Upon emergence from the Chapter&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="29306490" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">11</em> Case, we qualified for and adopted Fresh Start Accounting</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> in accordance with the provisions set forth in FASB ASC <em data-td-fact-id="29306491" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306492" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">852,</em> &ldquo;Reorganizations&rdquo; as (i) holders of existing shares of the Predecessor immediately before the Effective Date received less than <em data-td-fact-id="29306493" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">50</em> percent of the voting shares of the Successor entity and (ii) the reorganization value of the Successor was less than its post-petition liabilities and estimated allowed claims immediately before the Effective Date. Under Fresh Start Accounting, our balance sheet on the date of emergence reflects all of our assets and liabilities at their fair values. Our emergence and the adoption of Fresh Start Accounting resulted in a new reporting entity, or the Successor, for financial reporting purposes. To facilitate our discussion and analysis of our vessels, financial condition and results of operations herein, we refer to the reorganized company as the Successor for periods subsequent to <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2017 </em>and the Predecessor for periods prior to <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 15, 2017. </em>In addition, we adopted new accounting policies related to drydock expenditures and depreciation of our long-lived assets. See Note <em data-td-fact-id="29306494" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1.</em> As a result, our consolidated financial statements and the accompanying notes thereto after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2017 </em>are <em data-td-fact-id="29306495" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> comparable to our consolidated financial statements and the accompanying notes thereto prior to <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 15, 2017. </em>Our presentations herein include a &ldquo;black line&rdquo; division to delineate and reinforce this lack of comparability. The effects of the Plan and the application of Fresh Start Accounting were reflected in the consolidated balance sheet as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2017, </em>and the related adjustments thereto were recorded in the consolidated statement of operations for the Predecessor period ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2017. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

</div>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Reorganization Value</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">As part of Fresh Start Accounting, we were required to determine the Reorganization Value of the Successor upon emergence from the Chapter <em data-td-fact-id="29306496" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">11</em> Case. Reorganization value represents the fair value of the Successor&rsquo;s total assets prior to the consideration of liabilities and is intended to approximate the amount a willing buyer would pay for our assets immediately after a restructuring. The reorganization value, which was derived from the Successor&rsquo;s enterprise value, was allocated to our individual assets based on their estimated fair values (except for deferred income taxes) in accordance with FASB ASC <em data-td-fact-id="29306497" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306498" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">805,</em> &ldquo;Business Combinations.&rdquo; The amount of deferred income taxes recorded was determined in accordance with FASB ASC <em data-td-fact-id="29306499" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306500" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">740,</em> &ldquo;Income Taxes.&rdquo;</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Enterprise value represents the estimated fair value of our long-term debt and shareholders<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo; equity. The Successor&rsquo;s enterprise value, as approved by the Bankruptcy Court in support of the Plan, was estimated to be within a range of <em data-td-fact-id="29306501" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$300</em> million to <em data-td-fact-id="29306502" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$400</em> million. Based on the estimates and assumptions utilized in our Fresh Start Accounting process, we estimated the Successor&rsquo;s enterprise value to be approximately <em data-td-fact-id="29306503" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$336</em> million. Fair values are inherently subject to significant uncertainties and contingencies beyond our control. Accordingly, there can be <em data-td-fact-id="29306504" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> assurance that the estimates, assumptions, valuations, appraisals and financial projections will be realized, and actual results could vary materially. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">The following table reconciles the enterprise value to the estimated fair value of our Successor common stock as of the Effective Date (in thousands<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">, except shares outstanding):</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Our consolidated statements of operations for the Successor period ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and the Predecessor period ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2017 </em>include reorganization items which reflect gains recognized on the settlement of liabilities subject to compromise and costs and other expenses associated with the bankruptcy proceedings, principally professional fees as well as the Fresh Start Accounting adjustments. Similar costs that were incurred during the pre-petition periods have been reported as pre-petition restructuring charges in our consolidated statements of operations.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:36pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:7.2pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><i>V</i><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><i>aluation Process</i></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">The fair values of the Successor&rsquo;s assets were determined with the assistance of a <em data-td-fact-id="29306505" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em>-party valuation expert. The reorganization value was allocated to our individual assets and liabilities based on their estimated fair values. Our principal assets are our platform supply vessels. For purposes of estimating the fair value of our vessels we used a combination of the discounted cash flow method (income approach) that we discounted at rates ranging between <em data-td-fact-id="29306506" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">18%</em> to <em data-td-fact-id="29306507" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">29%,</em> the guideline public company method (market approach) and the cost approach. The income approach was utilized to estimate the fair value of vessels that generated positive returns on projected cash flows over the remaining economic useful life of the vessels. The market approach was used to estimate the fair value of vessels with projected cash flow losses. The fair value of our other personal property was determined utilizing cost approach adjusted, as needed, for asset type, age, physical deterioration and obsolescence.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">The spare parts inventory were valued primarily using a combination of either (i) a cost approach that incorporated depreciation and obsolescence to the extent applicable on an asset-by-asset basis or (ii) market data for comparable assets to the extent that such information was available. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">The remaining reorganization value is attributable to cash and cash equivalents and working capital assets including accounts receivable and prepaids. Accounts receivable were subjected to analysis on an individual basis and reserved to the extent appropriate. The remaining assets approximate their fair values on the Effective Date.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Liabilities on the Effective Date include borrowings under our Term Loan Facility, working capital liabilities, long-term deferred income tax, other long-term income taxes payable and other liabilities which are primarily multi-employer pension obligations. The fair value of borrowings under our Term Loan Facility was determined by reviewing the agreement governing the Term Loan Facility, analyzing the terms and comparing the interest rate to market rates. It was determined that the face value of the borrowings under our Term Loan Facility approximates fair value. See Note <em data-td-fact-id="29306508" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">5.</em> Our working capital liabilities are obligations in the ordinary course of business and their carrying amounts approximate their fair values. The multi-employer pension obligations were valued at the present value of amounts expected to be paid. Other income taxes payable reflects amounts expected to be paid for income tax related penalties and interest as well as liabilities for uncertain tax positions.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">The fair value of the Noteholder Warrants was determined utilizing the closing trading price of our common stock, subsequent to the Effective Date, less the <em data-td-fact-id="29306509" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.01</em> strike price. The fair value of the Equity Warrants was determined utilizing the Black Scholes Valuation model. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Although we believe the assumptions and estimates used to develop enterprise value and reorganization value are reasonable and appropriate, different assumptions and estimates could materially impact the analysis and resulting conclusions. The assumptions used in estimating these values are inherently uncertain and require judgment. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1522067248521" id="thunderdome-statement-849954">
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>(</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="29306540" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">3</em></b><b>) IMPAIRMENT CHARGES</b></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Reduction in Value of Long-lived Assets and Goodwill</i><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:7.2pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Our tangible long-lived assets consist primarily of vessels and construction-in-progress. We review l</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">ong-lived assets for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of such assets <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em><em data-td-fact-id="29306541" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> be recoverable. We assess potential impairment by comparing the carrying values of the long-lived assets to the undiscounted cash flows expected to be received from those assets. If impairment is indicated, we determine the amount of impairment expense by comparing the carrying value of the long-lived assets with their fair market value. We base our u</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">ndiscounted cash flow estimates on, among other things, historical results adjusted to reflect the best estimate of future operating performance. We obtain estimates of fair value of our vessels from independent appraisal firms. Management&rsquo;s assumptions are an inherent part of our asset impairment evaluation, and the use of different assumptions could produce results that differ from those reported. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
<div id="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">72</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; border: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000">
<div id="PGHDR" style="text-align: left; width: 100%">&nbsp;</div>
</div>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Beginning i<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">n late <em data-td-fact-id="29306542" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2014,</em> the oil and gas industry experienced a significant decline in the price of oil causing an industry-wide downturn that continues into <em data-td-fact-id="29306543" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018.</em> Prices continued to decline throughout <em data-td-fact-id="29306544" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em> and into <em data-td-fact-id="29306545" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016,</em> reaching a low of less than <em data-td-fact-id="29306546" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$30</em> per barrel in early <em data-td-fact-id="29306547" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016.</em> Prices began to recover over the remainder of <em data-td-fact-id="29306548" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016,</em> stabilizing at over <em data-td-fact-id="29306549" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$40</em> per barrel for much of the <em data-td-fact-id="29306550" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">second</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="29306551" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em> quarters of <em data-td-fact-id="29306552" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and further increasing to over <em data-td-fact-id="29306553" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$50</em> per barrel by year end. Prices are subject to significant uncertainty and continue to be volatile, declining again in early <em data-td-fact-id="29306554" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> before recovering to over <em data-td-fact-id="29306555" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$60</em> per barrel in <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 2018. </em></font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">The downturn of the last few years has significantly impacted the operational plans for oil companies, resulting in reduced expenditures for exploration and production activities, and consequently has adversely affected the drilling and support service sector. The decrease in day rates and utilization for offshore vessels has been significant. In addition, the independent appraisal firms have lowered the fair value estimates related to our vessels in each quarter since the <em data-td-fact-id="29306556" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">fourth</em> quarter of <em data-td-fact-id="29306557" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2014.</em> As a result of these factors, we have performed a number of reviews for impairment since the <em data-td-fact-id="29306558" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">fourth</em> quarter of <em data-td-fact-id="29306559" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2014.</em> </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">See the discussions below detailing our impairment analyses and processes for each of goodwill, long-lived assets, intangible assets, vessel components and assets held for sale. The components of reduction in value of assets are as follows (in thousands):</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:54pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:3.6pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:7.2pt;"><u>Goodwill</u><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><u> Impairment</u></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We completed a qualitative analysis of goodwill of the Predecessor in <em data-td-fact-id="29306560" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em> and determined that further testing was necessary. Our goodwill impairment evaluation indicated that the carrying value of the North Sea segment exceeded its fair value so that goodwill was potentially impaired. We then performed the <em data-td-fact-id="29306561" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">second</em> step of the goodwill impairment test, which involved calculating the implied fair value of our goodwill by allocating the fair value of the North Sea segment to all of the assets and liabilities (other than goodwill) and comparing it to the carrying amount of goodwill. To estimate the fair value of the reporting unit we used a <em data-td-fact-id="29306562" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">50%</em> weighting of the discounted cash flow method and a <em data-td-fact-id="29306563" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">50%</em> weighting of the public company guideline method in determining fair value of the North Sea reporting unit.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We determined that the implied fair value of our goodwill for the North Sea segment was less than its carrying value and recorded a <em data-td-fact-id="29306564" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$22.6</em> million impairment of the North Sea segment<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s goodwill. As a result of this impairment, we <em data-td-fact-id="29306565" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> longer have any goodwill.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:7.2pt;"><u>Long-Lived Asset Impairment</u></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">In the Predecessor <em data-td-fact-id="29306566" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em> period, we recorded <em data-td-fact-id="29306567" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$129.2</em> million of impairment expense related to our long-lived assets in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico, which is a part of our Americas segment. The impairment consisted of <em data-td-fact-id="29306568" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$115.5</em> million related to our vessels and <em data-td-fact-id="29306569" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$13.7</em> million related to our intangible asset. As a result of this impairment, we <em data-td-fact-id="29306570" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> longer have an intangible asset.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">In the Predecessor <em data-td-fact-id="29306571" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> period, we recorded an aggregate of <em data-td-fact-id="29306572" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$160.2</em> million of impairment expense related to our long-lived assets. Impairment charges totaled <em data-td-fact-id="29306573" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$94.5</em> million for the U.S. Gulf of Mexico and <em data-td-fact-id="29306574" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$15.9</em> million for the non-U.S. Americas, both part of the Americas segment. We also recorded impairment in Southeast Asia totaling <em data-td-fact-id="29306575" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$49.8</em> million.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:7.2pt;"><u>Vessel Component Impairment</u></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:39.6pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:7.2pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We have vessel components in our North Sea and Southeast Asia segments that we intend to sell. We recorded impairment based on <em data-td-fact-id="29306576" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em> party appraisals of the North Sea components totaling <em data-td-fact-id="29306577" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.4</em> million in the Predecessor <em data-td-fact-id="29306578" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em> period. Based on <em data-td-fact-id="29306579" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em> party valuations, we recorded impairment expense related to these assets totaling <em data-td-fact-id="29306580" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$2.6</em> million, consisting of <em data-td-fact-id="29306581" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$2.0</em> million in the North Sea and <em data-td-fact-id="29306582" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.6</em> million in Southeast Asia, in the Predecessor <em data-td-fact-id="29306583" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> period.</p>
</div>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1522067264531" id="thunderdome-statement-849956">
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>(</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="29306584" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">4</em></b><b>) VESSEL ACQUISITIONS, DISPOSITIONS AND NEW-BUILD PROGRAM</b></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">During <em data-td-fact-id="29306585" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016,</em> the Predecessor sold <em data-td-fact-id="29306586" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> older vessel from our North Sea region fleet and <em data-td-fact-id="29306587" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> vessels from our Southeast Asia fleet for combined proceeds of <em data-td-fact-id="29306588" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$6.5</em> million. The sales of these vessels generated a combined loss on sales of assets of <em data-td-fact-id="29306589" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$8.6</em> million. In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> March 2017, </em>the Predecessor sold <em data-td-fact-id="29306590" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">two</em> fast supply <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">vessels and recorded combined losses on sales of assets of <em data-td-fact-id="29306591" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$5.3</em> million.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">At <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2015, </em>we had <em data-td-fact-id="29306592" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">two</em> vessels under construction in the U.S. that were significantly delayed. In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> March 2016, </em>we resolved certain matters under dispute with the shipbuilder and reset the contract schedules so that we would take delivery of the <em data-td-fact-id="29306593" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">first</em> vessel in mid-<em data-td-fact-id="29306594" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and the <em data-td-fact-id="29306595" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">second</em> vessel in mid-<em data-td-fact-id="29306596" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> at which time a final payment of <em data-td-fact-id="29306597" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$26.0</em> million would be due. We took delivery of the <em data-td-fact-id="29306598" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">first</em> of these vessels during the <em data-td-fact-id="29306599" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">second</em> quarter of <em data-td-fact-id="29306600" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016.</em> Under the settlement, we could elect <em data-td-fact-id="29306601" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> to take delivery of the <em data-td-fact-id="29306602" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">second</em> vessel and forego the final payment, in which case the shipbuilder would retain the vessel. In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> May 2017, </em>we elected <em data-td-fact-id="29306603" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">to take the vessel. We have <em data-td-fact-id="29306604" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> further purchase obligations under such contract.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We had a vessel under construction in Norway that was scheduled to be completed and delivered during the <em data-td-fact-id="29306605" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">first</em> quarter of <em data-td-fact-id="29306606" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016;</em> however, in the <em data-td-fact-id="29306607" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">fourth</em> quarter of <em data-td-fact-id="29306608" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em> we amended our contract with the shipbuilder to delay delivery of the vessel until <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 2017. </em>Concurrently, in order to delay the payment of a substantial portion of the construction costs, we agreed to pay monthly installments through <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> May 2016 </em>totaling <em data-td-fact-id="29306609" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">92.2</em> million NOK (or approximately <em data-td-fact-id="29306610" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$11.0</em> million) and to pay a final installment on delivery in <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 2017 </em>of <em data-td-fact-id="29306611" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">195.0</em> million NOK (or approximately <em data-td-fact-id="29306612" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$23.3</em> million at delivery). We paid such final installment and took delivery of this vessel in <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 2017.</em></p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Credit Facility Agreement</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">On <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2017, </em>GulfMark Rederi AS, or Rederi, a subsidiary of GulfMark Offshore, Inc., entered into an agreement, or the Credit Facility Agreement, with DNB Bank ASA, New York Branch, as agent, DNB Capital LLC as revolving and swingline lender, and certain funds managed by Hayfin Capital Management LLP as term lenders, providing for <em data-td-fact-id="29306619" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">two</em> credit facilities: a senior secured revolving credit facility, or the Revolving Credit Facility, and a senior secured term loan facility, or the Term Loan Facility (or, together, the Facilities). The Revolving Credit Facility provides <em data-td-fact-id="29306620" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$25.0</em> million of borrowing capacity, including <em data-td-fact-id="29306621" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$12.5</em> million for swingline loans and <em data-td-fact-id="29306622" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$5.0</em> million for letter of credit. The Term Loan Facility provides a <em data-td-fact-id="29306623" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$100.0</em> million term loan, which was funded in full on the <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2017. </em>Borrowings under the Revolving Credit Facility <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be denominated in U.S. Dollars, NOK, GBP and Euros. Both Facilities mature on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2022. At December 31, 2017, we had $23.3 million of unused borrowing capacity under the Revolving Credit Facility.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Our costs incurred to negotiate and close the Credit Facility Agreement totaled <em data-td-fact-id="29306624" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$9.6</em> million. These costs are deferred and amortized into interest expense in our consolidated statements of operations. We attributed <em data-td-fact-id="29306625" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$7.8</em> million, or <em data-td-fact-id="29306626" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">80%,</em> of the debt issuance costs to the Term Loan Facility. These costs are amortized into interest expense using the effective interest method. The unamortized cost totaling <em data-td-fact-id="29306627" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$7.6</em> million at <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em>is presented in our consolidated balance sheets as an offset to our Term Loan Facility borrowing. We attributed <em data-td-fact-id="29306628" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.8</em> million, or <em data-td-fact-id="29306629" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">20%,</em> of the debt issuance costs to the Revolving Credit Facility. These costs are amortized into interest expense using the straight-line method over the term of the agreement. The unamortized cost totaling <em data-td-fact-id="29306630" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.7</em> million at <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em>is presented in our consolidated balance sheets in deferred costs and other assets.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Borrowings under the Facilities accrue interest on U.S. Dollar borrowings at our option using either (i)&nbsp;the adjusted U.S. prime rate, or ABR, plus <em data-td-fact-id="29306631" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">5.25%,</em> or (ii) the LIBOR Rate plus <em data-td-fact-id="29306632" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">6.25%.</em> NOK loans substitute LIBOR with an adjusted Norwegian offered quotation rate for deposits in NOK and Euro loans substitute LIBOR with an adjusted euro interbank offered rate administered by the European Money Markets Institute.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">At <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em>we had <em data-td-fact-id="29306633" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$100.0</em> million in borrowings outstanding under the Term Loan Facility and <em data-td-fact-id="29306634" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> borrowings outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility. At <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em>we had <em data-td-fact-id="29306635" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$25.0</em> million of borrowing capacity under the Revolving Credit Facility. At <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em>our weighted average interest rate on borrowings under the Term Loan Facility was <em data-td-fact-id="29306636" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">7.8%.</em> </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Repayment of borrowings under the Facilities is guaranteed by GulfMark Offshore, Inc. and each of its significant subsidiaries (or, collectively, with Rederi, the Obligors), and are secured by a lien on <em data-td-fact-id="29306637" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">27</em> collateral vessels, or the Collateral Vessels, and substantially all other assets of the Obligors.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Commitments under the Revolving Credit Facility will be reduced beginning on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2020 </em>in semiannual increments of approximately <em data-td-fact-id="29306638" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$3.1</em> million until maturity. The Term Loan Facility is payable in semiannual installments beginning on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2020 </em>and based on a <em data-td-fact-id="29306639" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">five</em>-year level principal payment schedule, payable semiannually.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Term Loan Facility prepayments prior to <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2019 </em>are subject to a make-whole premium based on the present value of interest otherwise payable from the prepayment date forward. Prepayments on or after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2019 </em>and prior to <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2020 </em>are subject to a <em data-td-fact-id="29306640" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2%</em> premium. Mandatory prepayments, other than those triggered by a casualty event, are subject to prepayment premiums. Mandatory prepayments are required upon the occurrence of certain events including, but <em data-td-fact-id="29306641" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> limited to, a change of control or the sale or total loss of a Collateral Vessel. Prepayments of the Revolving Credit Facility are <em data-td-fact-id="29306642" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> materially restricted or penalized.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">The Credit Facility Agreement was evaluated for embedded derivatives that must be bifurcated and separately accounted for as freestanding derivatives. The nature of any embedded features must be analyzed to determine whether each feature requires bifurcation by both (<em data-td-fact-id="29306643" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em>) meeting the definition of a derivative and (<em data-td-fact-id="29306644" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em>) <em data-td-fact-id="29306645" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> being considered clearly and closely related to the host contract. We have identified <em data-td-fact-id="29306646" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> features in the Credit Facility Agreement that are considered embedded derivatives. There is a contingent interest feature related to default interest, a breakage costs potential <em data-td-fact-id="29306647" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> related to prepayments, and certain potential contingent payments related to increased costs caused by changes in law. We determined that the value of these features are de minimis at the inception of the agreement and that we do <em data-td-fact-id="29306648" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> foresee events that would require a value adjustment in our consolidated financial statements. We will continue to assess the likelihood of triggering events and to the extent they are determined to be material, these features will be bifurcated from the debt instrument and subsequently marked to fair value through earnings.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">The Credit Facility Agreement contains financial covenants that require that we maintain: (i) minimum liquidity of <em data-td-fact-id="29306649" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$30.0</em> million, including <em data-td-fact-id="29306650" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$15.0</em> million in cash, (ii) a leverage ratio (total debt to <em data-td-fact-id="29306651" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">12</em> months EBITDA) of <em data-td-fact-id="29306652" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> more than <em data-td-fact-id="29306653" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">5.0</em> to <em data-td-fact-id="29306654" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1.0,</em> tested quarterly beginning <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2020, (</em>iii) a total debt to capital ratio, tested quarterly, <em data-td-fact-id="29306655" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> to exceed <em data-td-fact-id="29306656" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">0.45</em> to <em data-td-fact-id="29306657" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1.0,</em> and (iv) a collateral to commitment coverage ratio of at least <em data-td-fact-id="29306658" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2.50</em> to <em data-td-fact-id="29306659" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1.0.</em> The Credit Facility Agreement contains a number of restrictions that limit our ability to, among other things, sell Collateral Vessels, borrow money, make investments, incur additional liens on assets, buy or sell assets, merge, or pay dividends and contain a number of potential events of default related to our business, financial condition and vessel operations. Collateral Vessel operations are also subject to a variety of restrictive provisions. Proceeds from borrowings under the Credit Facility Agreement <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em><em data-td-fact-id="29306660" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> be used to acquire vessels or finance business acquisitions generally. At <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em>we were in compliance with all of the financial covenants under the Credit Facility Agreement.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
<div id="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">75</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; border: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000">
