<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The restrictions related to restricted stock awards terminated at the end of <em data-td-fact-id="29306864" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> years from the date of grant and the value of the restricted shares is amortized to expense over that period. Total amortization of stock-based compensation related to restricted stock was <em data-td-fact-id="29306865" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$2.6</em> million, <em data-td-fact-id="29306866" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$4.7</em><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">million and <em data-td-fact-id="29306867" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$5.9</em>&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">million for the Predecessor period ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2017 </em>and the years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December&nbsp;</em></font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="29306868" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">31,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306869" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="29306870" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015,</em> respectively. Total stock-based compensation for stock options was <em data-td-fact-id="29306871" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.2</em> million, <em data-td-fact-id="29306872" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.4</em> million and <em data-td-fact-id="29306873" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.6</em> million at <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2016 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="29306874" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015,</em> respectively. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>ESPP</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:14.4pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We had an employee stock purchase plan, or ESPP, that was available to all of our U.S. employees and certain subsidiaries, which we terminated in early <em data-td-fact-id="29306875" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017.</em> During the term of the ESPP, the employee contributions were used to acquire shares of the Predecessor<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s Class A common stock at <em data-td-fact-id="29306876" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">85%</em> of the fair market value of the Class A common stock. Total compensation expense related to the ESPP was <em data-td-fact-id="29306877" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.2</em>&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">million and <em data-td-fact-id="29306878" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.2</em>&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">million during the years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December&nbsp;</em></font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="29306879" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">31,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306880" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="29306881" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015,</em> respectively. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>U.K. ESPP</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Certain employees of our U.K. subsidiaries participated in a share incentive plan, which was similar to our ESPP but contained certain provisions designed to meet the requirements of the U.K. tax authorities. This plan was also terminated in early <em data-td-fact-id="29306882" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017.</em></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Deferred Compensation Plan</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We maintain a deferred compensation plan<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">, or DC Plan, under which a portion of the compensation for certain of our key employees, including officers, and non-employee directors, can be deferred for payment after retirement or termination of employment. Under the DC Plan, deferred compensation could be used to purchase our common stock or could be retained by us and earn interest at prime plus <em data-td-fact-id="29306883" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2%.</em> The <em data-td-fact-id="29306884" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">first</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306885" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">7.5%</em> of compensation deferred is required to be used to purchase the common stock and is matched by us. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We have established a &ldquo;Rabbi&rdquo; trust to hold the stock portion of benefits under the DC Plan. The funds provided to the trust are invested by a trustee independent of us in our common stock, which is purchased by the trustee on the open market. The assets of the trust are available to satisfy the claims of all general creditors in the event of bankruptcy or insolvency. Dividend equivalents are paid on the stock units at the same rate as dividends on our common stock and are re-invested as additional stock units based upon the fair market value of a share of our common stock on the date of payment of the dividend.<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b><i> </i></b><b><i> </i></b>On the Effective Date, the DC Plan received Successor common stock and Equity Warrants that were issued pursuant to the Plan in exchange for the Predecessor Class A common stock previously held by the trust. Accordingly, the Successor common stock held by the trust and our liabilities under the DC Plan are included in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets as treasury stock and deferred compensation expense.</font></p>
</div>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="12876" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1522067368364" id="thunderdome-statement-849975">
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>(</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="29306886" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">10</em></b><b>) EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS</b></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><em data-td-fact-id="29306887" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">401</em>(k)</i><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> <i>Plan</i></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We offer a <em data-td-fact-id="29306888" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">401</em>(k) plan to all of our U.S. employees and provide matching contribution to those employees that participate. The matching contributions paid by us totaled <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="29306889" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.0</em>&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">million for the year ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December&nbsp;</em></font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="29306890" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">31,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306891" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015.</em> In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> August 2015, </em>we suspended the matching contribution.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Multi-employer Pension Obligation<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Certain of our current and former U.K. subsidiaries are participating in a multi-employer retirement fund known as the Merchant Navy Officers Pension Fund, or MNOPF.<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp; At <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December&nbsp;</em><em data-td-fact-id="29306892" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">31,</em>&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="29306893" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> the Successor had accrued <em data-td-fact-id="29306894" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.2</em> million related to this liability, which reflects the present value of all obligations assessed on us by the fund&rsquo;s trustee as of such date. This figure is the same as was accrued by the Predecessor at <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2017. </em>We continue to have employees who participate in the MNOPF and will as a result continue to make routine payments to the fund as those employees accrue additional benefits over time.&nbsp; The status of the fund is calculated by an actuarial firm every <em data-td-fact-id="29306895" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> years. The last assessment was completed in <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> March 2015 </em>and resulted in a significantly improved funding position, mainly due to hedging the interest rate and inflation risk, to between <em data-td-fact-id="29306896" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">65%</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="29306897" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">80%.</em>&nbsp; The reported net deficit of the fund at <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> March 31, 2015 </em>was <em data-td-fact-id="29306898" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$7.5</em> million and, as a result, the MNOPF trustee did <em data-td-fact-id="29306899" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> propose to collect any additional deficit contributions related to the new deficit.&nbsp; The amount and timing of additional potential future obligations relating to underfunding depend on a number of factors, but principally on future fund performance and the underlying actuarial assumptions. Our share of the fund&rsquo;s deficit is dependent on a number of factors including future actuarial valuations, asset performance, the number of participating employers, and the final method used in allocating the required contribution among participating employers. In addition, our obligation could increase if other employers <em data-td-fact-id="29306900" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> longer participated in the plan. In the Predecessor period ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2017 </em>and for the years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December</em><b>&nbsp;</b><em data-td-fact-id="29306901" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">31,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306902" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="29306903" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015,</em> the Predecessor made deficit contributions to the plan of <em data-td-fact-id="29306904" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.4</em> million, <em data-td-fact-id="29306905" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.4</em> million and <em data-td-fact-id="29306906" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.4</em> million, respectively.&nbsp; In the Successor period ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017 </em>we made <em data-td-fact-id="29306907" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> additional contribution. Our contributions do <em data-td-fact-id="29306908" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> make up more than <em data-td-fact-id="29306909" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">five</em>&nbsp;percent of total contributions to the plan. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
<div id="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">83</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; border: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000">
<div id="PGHDR" style="text-align: left; width: 100%">&nbsp;</div>
</div>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">In addition, we participate in the Merchant Navy Ratings Pension Fund, or MNRPF, in a capacity similar to our participation in the MNOPF.<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp; Prior to <em data-td-fact-id="29306910" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2013,</em> we were <em data-td-fact-id="29306911" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> required to contribute to any deficit in the MNRPF. Due to a change in the plan rules, however, we were advised that we would be required to make contributions beginning in <em data-td-fact-id="29306912" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2013.</em>&nbsp; As of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2017, </em>the Predecessor had accrued <em data-td-fact-id="29306913" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.8</em> million for this fund. The most recent actuarial valuation was completed as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> March 31, 2017 </em>and deficit information was communicated in the <em data-td-fact-id="29306914" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">fourth</em> quarter of <em data-td-fact-id="29306915" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017.</em> Our share of the deficit was calculated at <em data-td-fact-id="29306916" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.5</em> million for which we expect to receive a formal payment demand in the <em data-td-fact-id="29306917" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em> quarter of <em data-td-fact-id="29306918" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018.</em>&nbsp; As of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em>the amount of the MNRPF accrual recorded by the Successor was adjusted to <em data-td-fact-id="29306919" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.6</em> million, which is a combination of the deficit mentioned above plus an estimate of further deficit amounts from <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> April 2017 </em>onward. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Norwegian Pension Plans</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Norwegian benefit pension plans include approximately <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="29306920" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">144</em> of our employees, primarily seamen, and are defined benefit, multiple-employer plans, insured with Nordea Liv. We also instituted a defined contribution plan in <em data-td-fact-id="29306921" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2008</em> for shore-based personnel that existing personnel could elect to participate in while discontinuing any further obligations in the defined benefit plan. All newly hired shore-based personnel are required to join the defined contribution plan. Benefits under the defined benefit plans are based primarily on participants&rsquo; years of credited service, wage level at age of retirement and the contribution from the Norwegian National Insurance. A <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December&nbsp;</em></font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="29306922" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">31,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306923" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> measurement date is used for the actuarial computation of the defined benefit pension plans. The following tables provide information about changes in the benefit obligation and plan assets and the funded status of the Norwegian defined benefit pension plans (in thousands):</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The vested benefit obligation is calculated as the actuarial present value of the vested benefits to which employees are currently entitled based on the employees<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo; expected date of separation or retirement.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The investment strategy focuses on providing a stable return on plan assets using a diversified portfolio of investments.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The projected benefit obligation and the fair value of plan assets for the Norwegian pension plan were approximately <em data-td-fact-id="29306924" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$5.</em><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="29306925" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">5</em> million and <em data-td-fact-id="29306926" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$5.6</em> million, respectively, as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="29306927" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$5.2</em>&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">million and <em data-td-fact-id="29306928" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$5.5</em>&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">million, respectively, as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December&nbsp;</em><em data-td-fact-id="29306929" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">31,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306930" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016.</em>&nbsp;The accumulated benefit obligation was <em data-td-fact-id="29306931" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$4.8</em> million and <em data-td-fact-id="29306932" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$4.8</em> million as of December <em data-td-fact-id="29306933" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">31,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306934" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="29306935" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016,</em> respectively. We expect to contribute approximately <em data-td-fact-id="29306936" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.4</em>&nbsp;million to the Norwegian pension plan in <em data-td-fact-id="29306937" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306938" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No</em> plan assets are expected to be returned to us in <em data-td-fact-id="29306939" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018.</em> </font></p>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="12877" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1522067384725" id="thunderdome-statement-849983">
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>(<em data-td-fact-id="29306940" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em></b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="29306941" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em></b><b>) STOCKHOLDERS&rsquo; EQUITY</b></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Common Stock</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">All the Predecessor&rsquo;s Class A common stock was cancelled upon our emergence from bankruptcy on the Effective Date in exchange for <em data-td-fact-id="29306942" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">75,000</em> shares of Successor common stock and <em data-td-fact-id="29306943" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">810,811</em> Equity Warrants.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">We have authority to issue <em data-td-fact-id="29306944" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">25,000,000</em> shares of common st<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">ock. We are subject to U.S. maritime laws that generally require that only U.S. citizens own and operate U.S.-flag vessels for trade between points in the United States. &nbsp;Our Certificate of Incorporation provides that <em data-td-fact-id="29306945" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> shares of any class or series of our capital stock <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be transferred to a Non-U.S. Citizen (as therein defined) if, upon completion of such transfer, the number of shares beneficially owned by all Non-U.S. Citizens in the aggregate would exceed the <em data-td-fact-id="29306946" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">24%,</em> or the Permitted Percentage, of the total issued and outstanding shares. The shares of such class or series of capital stock beneficially owned by Non-U.S. Citizens in excess of the Permitted Percentage are referred to as Excess Shares. To prevent the percentage of aggregate shares of our capital stock owned by Non-U.S. Citizens from exceeding the Permitted Percentage, we, at our sole discretion, will have the power to redeem all or any number of such Excess Shares. We have the option to redeem the Excess Share for: (i) cash; (ii) Redemption Warrants, which are warrants to purchase <em data-td-fact-id="29306947" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> share of our common stock at <em data-td-fact-id="29306948" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$.01</em> per share and do <em data-td-fact-id="29306949" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> give the holder any rights as a shareholder; or (iii) Redemption Notes, which are interest-bearing promissory notes with a maturity date of <em data-td-fact-id="29306950" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">ten</em> years or less. Until such Excess Shares are redeemed, or they are <em data-td-fact-id="29306951" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> longer Excess Shares, the holders of such shares will <em data-td-fact-id="29306952" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> be entitled to any voting rights with respect to such Excess Shares and we will pay any dividends or distributions with respect to such Excess Shares, if any, into a segregated account. </font></p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><i>Noteholder Warrants </i></font></p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">The Jones Act, which applies to companies that engage in maritime transportation of merchandise and passengers between points in the United States, requires that, among other thin<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">gs, with respect to a publicly traded company, the aggregate ownership of common stock by Non-U.S. Citizens be <em data-td-fact-id="29306953" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> more than <em data-td-fact-id="29306954" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">25%</em> of its outstanding common stock. Accordingly, Non-U.S. Citizen creditors who would otherwise be recipients of Successor common stock pursuant to the Plan or the Rights Offerings received, in lieu of Successor common stock, Noteholder Warrants to acquire Successor common stock at an exercise price of <em data-td-fact-id="29306955" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$.01</em> per share.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">On the Effective Date, we entered into a warrant agreement, pur<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">suant to which we issued the Noteholder Warrants entitling the holders thereof to purchase an aggregate of <em data-td-fact-id="29306956" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2,956,859</em> shares of Successor common stock. The Noteholder Warrants are exercisable for a <em data-td-fact-id="29306957" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">25</em>-year term commencing on the Effective Date at an exercise price of <em data-td-fact-id="29306958" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$.01</em> per share. Any outstanding Noteholder Warrant that has <em data-td-fact-id="29306959" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> been exercised upon maturity of the Noteholder Warrants on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2042 </em>will be exchanged for Redemption Warrants that will be substantially in the same form of the existing Noteholder Warrants. <em data-td-fact-id="29306960" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No</em> Noteholder Warrants were exercised during the period from <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 15, 2017 </em>to <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Equity Warrants </i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">On the Effective Date, we entered into a warrant agreement, pursuant to which we issued the Equity Warrants entitling the holders thereof to purchase an aggregate of <em data-td-fact-id="29306961" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">810,811</em> shares of Successor common stock, exercisable for a <em data-td-fact-id="29306962" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">7</em>-year period commencing on the Effective Date at an exercise price of <em data-td-fact-id="29306963" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$100.00</em> per share, subject to adjustment as described in the warrant agreement for the Equity Warrants.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">The Equity Warrants contain certain provisions to facilitate our compliance with the U.S. Maritime Laws limiting the ownership of our common stock by Non-U.S. Citizens. <em data-td-fact-id="29306964" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No</em> Equity Warrants were exercised during the period from <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 15, 2017 </em>to <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017.</em></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<div id="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">86</div>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Common Stock Issuances</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">During <em data-td-fact-id="29306965" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="29306966" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> proceeds were received from the issuance of the Predecessor&rsquo;s Class A common stock. During <em data-td-fact-id="29306967" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306968" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">165,849</em> shares of Predecessor&rsquo;s Class A common stock were issued, generating approximately <em data-td-fact-id="29306969" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.4</em> million in proceeds. During <em data-td-fact-id="29306970" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306971" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">101,179</em> shares of Predecessor&rsquo;s Class A common stock were issued generating approximately <em data-td-fact-id="29306972" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.7</em> million in proceeds. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Preferred Stock</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We are authorized by our Certificate of Incorporation, as amended, to issue up to <em data-td-fact-id="29306973" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">5,000,000</em> shares of preferred stock, <em data-td-fact-id="29306974" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$.01</em> par value per share. <em data-td-fact-id="29306975" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No</em> such shares have been issued.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Stock Repurchases</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 2012, </em>the Predecessor Board of Directors approved a stock repurchase program for up to a total of <em data-td-fact-id="29306976" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$100.0</em> million of our issued and outstanding Predecessor Class A common stock. <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">We did <em data-td-fact-id="29306977" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> repurchase any Predecessor Class A common stock in <em data-td-fact-id="29306978" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="29306979" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> or <em data-td-fact-id="29306980" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015.</em> </font></p>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="12878" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1522067398322" id="thunderdome-statement-849984">
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>(<em data-td-fact-id="29306981" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em></b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="29306982" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em></b><b>) OPERATING SEGMENT INFORMATION</b></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Business Segments</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We operate our business based on geographic locations and maintain th<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">ree operating segments: the North Sea, Southeast Asia and the Americas. Our chief operating decision-maker regularly reviews financial information about each of these operating segments in deciding how to allocate resources and evaluate performance. The business within each of these geographic regions has similar economic characteristics, services, distribution methods and regulatory concerns. All of the operating segments are considered reportable segments under FASB ASC <em data-td-fact-id="29306983" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="29306984" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">280,</em> <i>&ldquo;Segment Reporting.&rdquo;</i></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:14.4pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
<div id="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">87</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; border: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000">
<div id="PGHDR" style="text-align: left; width: 100%">&nbsp;</div>
</div>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Management evaluates segment performance primarily based on operating income. Cash and debt are managed centrally. Because the regions do <em data-td-fact-id="29306985" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> manage those items, the gains and losses on foreign currency remeasurements associated with these items are excluded from operating income. Management considers segment operating income to be a good indicator of each segment&rsquo;s operating performance from its continuing operations, as it represents the results of the ownership interest in operations without regard to financing methods or capital structures. All significant transactions between segments are conducted on an arms-length basis based on prevailing market prices and are accounted for as such. Operating income and other information regularly provided to our chief operating decision-maker is summarized in the following table (all amounts in thousands):</font></p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:49.7pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;">(a)&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Vessels under construction are included in other<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> assets until delivered. Revenue, long-lived assets and capital expenditures presented in the table above are allocated to segments based on the location where the vessel is employed, which in some instances differs from the segment where the vessel is legally owned. For the Successor period from <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 15, 2017 </em>through <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em>we had <em data-td-fact-id="29306986" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$3.4</em> million in revenue and <em data-td-fact-id="29306987" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$91.7</em> million in long-lived assets attributed to the United States, our country of domicile. In the Predecessor period from <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2017 </em>through <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2017, </em>we had <em data-td-fact-id="29306988" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$16.5</em> million in revenue attributed to the United States. In <em data-td-fact-id="29306989" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016,</em> we had <em data-td-fact-id="29306990" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$28.5</em>&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">million in revenue and <em data-td-fact-id="29306991" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$371.6</em> million in long-lived assets attributed to the United States, our country of domicile. In <em data-td-fact-id="29306992" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015,</em> we had <em data-td-fact-id="29306993" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$73.4</em> million in revenue and <em data-td-fact-id="29306994" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$431.7</em> million in long-lived assets attributed to the United States. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>ITEM 9. </b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b><i>Changes in and Disagreements with Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure</i></b></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt;">None.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>ITEM 9A. </b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b><i>Controls and Procedures</i></b> </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Disclosure Controls and Procedures</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">We maintain disclosure controls and procedures that are designed to provide reasonable assurance that information required to be disclosed in our reports under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC&rsquo;s rules and forms, and that such information is accumulated and communicated to management, including our Principal Executive Officer and Principal Financial Officer, as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. Our management, with the participation of our Principal Executive Officer and Principal Financial Officer, has evaluated the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures as of the end of the Predecessor period ended November 14, 2017 and the Successor period ended December 31, 2017, both of which are covered by this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Our Principal Executive Officer and Principal Financial Officer have concluded that, as of the end of each such period covered by this Annual Report on Form 10-K, our disclosure controls and procedures were effective at the reasonable assurance level.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Management<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s Annual Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting, as defined in Exchange Act Rule 13a-15(f). Our internal control over financial reporting is a process designed under the supervision of our Principal Executive Officer and Principal Financial Officer to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of our financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Our management assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting at <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">November 14, 2017 for the Predecessor and at December 31, 2017 for the Successor, and in making this assessment, used the criteria set forth by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) in <i>Internal Control-Integrated Framework (2013)</i>. Based on this assessment, management determined that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of November 14, 2017 for the Predecessor and as of December 31, 2017 for the Successor. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">There are inherent limitations to the effectiveness of any control system, however well designed, including the possibility of human error or mistakes, faulty judgments in decision-making and the possible circumvention or overriding of controls. Further, the design of a control system must reflect the fact that there are resource constraints, and the benefits of controls must be considered relative to their costs. Management must make judgments with respect to the relative cost and expected benefits of any specific control measure. The design of a control system also is based in part upon assumptions and judgments made by management about the likelihood of future events, and there can be no assurance that a control will be effective under all potential future conditions. As a result, even an effective system of internal controls can provide no more than reasonable assurance with respect to the fair presentation of financial statements and the processes under which they were prepared. Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because if changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies and procedures may deteriorate.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:14.4pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Changes in Internal Control </b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b>over</b><b> Financial Reporting</b></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">During the Predecessor period ended November 14, 2017, we implemented a change in internal control over financial reporting related to review of the calculation and reconciliation of income tax provision and related accounts. This change was implemented to remediate a material weakness in process level controls over management review of the calculation and reconciliation of income tax provision and related accounts. This material weakness arose in prior Predecessor periods and resulted in a calculation error that, while not material to the Predecessor&rsquo;s consolidated financial statements, could have accumulated to a material amount. To remediate this deficiency, the Predecessor employed a third-party expert to assist with the review of the calculation and reconciliation of income tax provision and related accounts. This material weakness did not have a pervasive effect on internal control over financial reporting for the Predecessor, as it was limited only to review of the calculation, allocation and reconciliation of income taxes and had no effect over internal control over financial reporting for the Successor.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">There were no other changes in our internal control over financial reporting during the Predecessor period beginning October 1, 2017 and ended November 14, 2017, or the Successor period ended December 31, 2017 </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">that materially affected, or would be reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting in either period.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>ITEM 9B. </b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b><i>Other Information</i></b> </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">On October 26, 2017, we reported, under Item 5.02 of our Current Report on Form 8-K filed on October 26, 2017, the departure of our Senior Vice President <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&ndash; General Counsel and Secretary, Cindy M. Muller, effective as of October 20, 2017. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">On January 16, 2018, we entered into a Separation and General Release Agreement with Ms. Muller, or the Muller Separation Agreement. Under the Muller Separation Agreement, Ms. Muller received approximately $144,312 (representing six months of her base salary and three months of welfare benefit continuation) in full satisfaction of our obligations to her under our Severance Benefits Policy, as in effect at the time of her termination, and the Change of Control Agreement, dated March 17, 2017, between us and Ms. Muller, or the Change of Control Agreement. The Muller Separation Agreement also contains a general release and subjects Ms. Muller to a three-month non-competition provision and customary confidentiality and non-solicitation covenants. A copy of the Muller Separation Agreement is filed as Exhibit 10.19 to this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Eugene Davis is the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of PIRINATE Consulting Group, LLC, a firm he founded in 1999. In this capacity, he has managed numerous debtor and creditor side pre- and post-restructuring assignments in several industries including the oil and gas sector.<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp; In addition, Mr. Davis has 35 years of experience in the oil and gas industry, including as an exploration and production attorney at Exxon Corporation and an international negotiator at Standard Oil Company (Indiana) (Amoco). He currently serves as chairman of the board of Atlas Iron Limited, an ASX-listed mining company; chairman of the board of U.S. Concrete, Inc., a NASDAQ-listed concrete company; as co-chairman of the board and member of the corporate governance and nominating committee of Verso Corporation, an NYSE-listed paper company; as chairman of the audit &amp; finance committee of VICI Properties Inc.; and as a director of Titan Energy, LLC, an exploration and production company trading on the OTC Markets. During the past five years, Mr. Davis has also been a director of the following publicly traded companies: Atlas Air Worldwide Holdings, Inc.; The Cash Store Financial Services, Inc.; Dex One Corp.; Genco Shipping &amp; Trading Limited; Global Power Equipment Group, Inc.; Goodrich Petroleum Corp.; Great Elm Capital Corporation; GSI Group, Inc.; Hercules Offshore, Inc.; HRG Group, Inc.; Knology, Inc.; SeraCare Life Sciences, Inc.; Spansion, Inc.; Spectrum Brands Holdings, Inc.; and WMIH Corp. He has also served on numerous boards of companies in the oil and gas industry, including Texas American Resources Company; Trident Exploration Corp.; Throne Petroleum; Magnum Hunter Resources Corp.; Hercules Offshore, Inc.; Stallion Oilfield Services; Warren Resources, Inc.; Coho Energy Inc.; and PetroRig. His experience in serving on numerous public and private company boards provides valuable insight into the business and financial decisions that come before our Board.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Domenic DiPiero is the Founder of Newport Capital Group, a national investment advisory firm, and has served as its President since 2004. With over twenty years of experience in the petroleum industry in shipping and marketing, Mr. DiPiero previously served as the President of Dove Terminals, a bulk petroleum storage company, from <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">1993 until 2005. He is also the former President of Delphi Petroleum Bunkering Division, where he was responsible for the supply and marketing of ship fuels in the U.S. representing Exxon from 2000 until 2004. He previously served as the President of the Marketing Division of Delphi Petroleum, a global energy trading firm specializing in the distribution of physical petroleum from 1994 until 2000. Mr. DiPiero served on the boards of Delphi Petroleum, Inc. from 2004 until 2015, and Zipz, Inc. from 2014 until the present. He served as chairman of the board of the Meridian Health System Foundation in 2012, and the Riverview Medical Center Foundation from 2011 until 2012. Since 2012, Mr. DiPiero has served as a Trustee of Drexel University. His extensive knowledge of the shipping and oil and gas services industries, his experience as a director of various companies, his banking experience and his financial and executive management expertise, provide Mr. DiPiero unique insight into the business decisions that come before our Board.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Quintin V. Kneen is our President and Chief Executive Officer. He was named our Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer in 2009 and served in those roles until he was appointed as our President and Chief Executive Officer in June 2013. Mr. Kneen joined GulfMark in June 2008 as Vice President <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&ndash; Finance and was named Senior Vice President &ndash; Finance and Administration in December 2008. Previously, he was Vice President &ndash; Finance &amp; Investor Relations for Grant Prideco, Inc., serving in executive finance positions at Grant Prideco since 2003. Prior to joining Grant Prideco, Mr. Kneen held executive finance positions at Azurix Corp. and was an Audit Manager with the Houston office of Price Waterhouse LLP. He holds a Master of Business Administration from Rice University and a Bachelor of Business Administration in Accounting from Texas A&amp;M University and is a Certified Public Accountant and a Chartered Financial Analyst. Mr. Kneen&rsquo;s extensive financial expertise and his position as our President and Chief Executive Officer provide him with unique personal knowledge and experience regarding our Company and its operations.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Scott McCarty is a partner of Q Investments and has been with Q Investments since 2002. Prior to his current position as manager of the venture capital, private equity and distressed investment groups, he was a portfolio manager. Before joining Q Investments, Mr. McCarty was a captain in the United States Army. Mr. McCarty has served as a member of the compensation committee of Vantage Drilling International since February 2016 and has served as a member of the nominating and corporate governance committee of Jones Energy, Inc., an NYSE-listed oil and gas exploration and development company, since February 2018. He previously served as a member of the compensation committee of Travelport Worldwide Limited, an NYSE-listed technology company, from May 2013 until November 2014. Mr. McCarty<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s experience gained from serving as a director of public companies, his military experience and his extensive background in finance provide valuable insight into business deliberations and decisions that come before our Board.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Louis Raspino<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s career has spanned almost 40 years in the energy industry, most recently as Chairman of Clarion Offshore Partners, a partnership with Blackstone that served as its platform for pursuing worldwide investments in the offshore oil &amp; gas services sector, from October 2015 until October 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp; Mr. Raspino served as President, Chief Executive Officer and a director of Pride International, Inc. from June 2005 until the company merged with Ensco plc in May 2011 and as its Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer from December 2003 until June 2005. From July&nbsp;2001 until December&nbsp;2003, he served as Senior Vice President, Finance and Chief Financial Officer of Grant Prideco, Inc. and from February 1999 until March 2001, he served as Vice President of Finance at Halliburton. Prior to joining Haliburton, Mr. Raspino served as Senior Vice President at Burlington Resources, Inc. from October 1997 until July 1998. From 1978 until its merger with Burlington Resources, Inc. in 1997, he held a variety of positions at Louisiana Land and Exploration Company, most recently as Senior Vice President, Finance and Administration and Chief Financial Officer. Mr. Raspino previously served as a director of Chesapeake Energy Corporation and chairman of its audit committee from March 2013 until March 2016, and as a director of Dresser-Rand Group, Inc., where he served as chairman of the compensation committee and member of the audit committee, from December 2005 until its merger into Siemens in June 2015. He has served as a director of Forum Energy Technologies, an NYSE-listed global oilfield products company, since January 2012 and currently serves as the chairman of its compensation committee.&nbsp; Mr. Raspino also currently serves on the board of The American Bureau of Shipping, where he is a member of the audit and compensation committees.&nbsp; Mr. Raspino&rsquo;s experience gained from his executive leadership roles for energy companies, including as chief executive officer and chief financial officer, and on various oil and gas industry boards, provides in-depth operational and financial expertise to our Board.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Krishna Shivram is the Chief Executive Officer and a director of Sentinel Energy Services Inc., a NASDAQ-listed special purpose acquisition company, that had a successful IPO in November 2017. Previously, Mr. Shivram served as the Interim Chief Executive Officer of Weatherford International PLC, an NYSE-listed oil and gas services company, from November 2016 to March 2017 and as its Chief Financial Officer from November 2013 to November 2016. From February 1988 to October 2013, Mr. Shivram held various positions at Schlumberger Limited, an NYSE-listed oil and gas services company, including Vice President and Treasurer, Controller and Head of M&amp;A. Prior to joining Schlumberger, Mr. Shivram held positions with public accounting firms Arthur Andersen and Ernst &amp; Young. Since August 2017, Mr. Shivram has served as the chairman of the audit committee of Ranger Energy Services, an NYSE-listed oilfield services company. Mr. Shivram<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s extensive executive management background with NYSE-listed oil and gas services companies provides valuable industry insight relevant to many of the business decisions that come before our Board.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Kenneth Traub has served as a Managing Partner of Raging Capital Management, LLC, a diversified investment firm, since December 2015. Prior to joining Raging Capital Management, LLC, he served as President and Chief Executive Officer of Ethos Management, LLC from 2009 through 2015. Mr. Traub has served as Chairman of the Board of DSP Group, Inc., a NASDAQ-listed leading supplier of wireless chipset solutions for converged communications, since <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">2012, Intermolecular, Inc., a NASDAQ-listed innovator in materials sciences, since 2016 and IDW Media Holdings, Inc. a diversified media company, since 2016, each of which is a Raging Capital Management, LLC portfolio company. Mr. Traub has previously served on the boards of numerous companies including MIPS Technologies, Inc., a provider of industry standard processor architectures and cores, from 2011 until 2013, Xyratex Limited, a leading supplier of data storage technologies, from 2013 until 2014, Vitesse Semiconductor Corporation, a supplier of integrated circuit solutions for next-generation carrier and enterprise networks, from 2013 until 2015, Athersys, Inc., a biotechnology company engaged in the discovery and development of therapeutic product candidates, from 2012 to 2016, A. M. Castle &amp; Co., a specialty metals distribution company from, 2014 to 2016 and MRV Communications, Inc., a supplier of communication networking equipment, from 2011 until 2017. Mr. Traub&rsquo;s extensive management background and experience serving on a wide variety of corporate boards enable Mr. Traub to provide valuable financial and transactional expertise and insight to our Board.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>SECTION 16(a) BENEFICIAL OWNERSHIP REPORTING COMPLIANCE</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Section 16(a) of the Exchange Act requires our officers and directors, and persons who own more than 10% of our common stock, par value $.01 per share, or Common Stock, to file reports of ownership and changes in ownership with the SEC. Officers, directors and greater than 10% stockholders are required by the regulation to furnish us with copies of all Section 16(a) reports they file.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>ITEM 11. </b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b><i>Executive Compensation</i></b> </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>COMPENSATION OVERVIEW </b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">This Compensation Overview provides information regarding the 2017 compensation program in place for (i) our President and Chief Executive Officer, (ii) our two other most highly-compensated executive officers serving as of December 31, 2017 and (iii) Ms. Muller, who would have been one of our two other most highly-compensated executive officers but for the fact that she departed effective as of October 20, 2017 and was no longer serving as of December 31, 2017, whom we refer to collectively as our named executive officers. This section includes information regarding our compensation philosophy and objectives, the components of our compensation program, and the key factors the Board, the Compensation Committee and our President and Chief Executive Officer considered in determining the compensation for our named executive officers in 2017. For 2017, our named executive officers were: </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>
